content:
"Walkinshaw was taken into police custody and placed in the back of a caged police vehicle while officers dealt with the crash and the injured passenger. But the coroner later found that the vehicle, like others in use across the Northern Territory, had no effective CCTV monitoring despite repeated warnings that people were attempting to harm themselves inside them.

According to the findings, Walkinshaw was left alone in the van long enough to hang himself using his own clothing. By the time officers noticed something was wrong, he was already unconscious. He was rushed to hospital but died the next day.

The coroner said the death was preventable and laid much of the blame on police inaction. An internal recommendation to install CCTV in caged vehicles had been made years earlier after another man died in custody, yet nothing was done. Instead, the risks kept mounting, with multiple incidents of detainees trying to take their own lives in the back of vans.

Cavanagh described the repeated failures as deeply troubling, saying police had been warned clearly enough that the danger was obvious. The report urged urgent changes to custody transport procedures, including better surveillance, improved risk assessment and faster intervention when vulnerable people are detained.

For Walkinshaw’s family, the findings confirmed what they had feared: that their son’s death was not simply the result of a tragic moment, but of a system that had already shown signs of breaking down and was allowed to continue unchanged."
